To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the photoactive layer of OPV device can be well characterized by the combination of several important morphological characterization tools and a novel analytical method, which is able to quantitatively evaluate temperature dependent miscibilities of organic material blends.

(1) The combination of several important characterization tools provides a comprehensive picture of the photoactive morphology and its correlation to the device performance, (2) the highly quantitative morphological data given by R SoX S and STXM are essential to the morphology property performance correlation, and (3) the analytical method based on optical microscopy and absorption can be utilized to predict morphology development at certain conditions and help to design better materials.

(1) the combination of soft X ray scattering and microscopy tools provides highly quantitative information about morphology of photoactive layer; (2) the morphology property performance correlation based on the combination is capable of providing guidance to device design; (3) the novel analytical method based combination of optical microscopy with absorption can be applied to evaluate the miscibility and molecular interaction parameters of material blends and to predict the morphology development at a certain temperature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the morphology-property-performance relationship in organic photovoltaics (OPV) and the morphology evolution of the photoactive layers in the fabrication process.
the characterization and prediction of photoactive layer morphology for organic photovoltaics.
the morphology characterization and the morphology performance correlation of organic photovoltaic devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the morphology-property-performance relationship of organic solar cells is not a simple one, it is a complex and dynamic one.

the morphology of the photoactive layers is the key factor that determines the device performance, which can be quantitatively characterized by the combination of several important characterization tools.

the morphology characterization tools are capable of providing detailed and quantitative information about photoactive layer morphology, which are crucial for device design, optimization, and understanding.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the combination of several powerful morphology characterization techniques and the development of a novel analytical method provide the detailed and quantitative information about the morphology of photoactive layer, and thus enable us to understand and control the morphology development during the device fabrication process.
the morphology characterization tools are capable of providing detailed and comprehensive morphologies of the organic photovoltaic devices and the morphology property correlation is well established.

the photoactive layer of organic photovoltaic devices is composed of two phases with different molecular packing and orientation, which can be characterized by a series of morphology characterization tools.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a constructive combination of several morphology characterization tools makes possible to provide the comprehensive morphological pictures of the photoactive layers and to construct the morphology-property-performance correlation.
the combination of several morphology characterization tools can provide the detailed and complete morphological pictures about OPV photoactive layer.
